evals.name: red-exposes-contract-ambiguity
evals.prompt: The first failing test reveals two plausible 404 response contracts, and neither the accepted brief nor ADR chooses one. Continue with the safest next action.
evals.expected_output: Pause the RED slice and hand the failing example plus contract decision to design instead of encoding a guess.
assertions: Names engineering-design-thinking as the next owner
Carries the failing example, alternatives, and decision needed
Does not guess the public contract

evals.name: green-exposes-broader-candidate
evals.prompt: The accepted behavior slice is green. It exposed duplicated repository ownership across three features outside the approved scope. Continue without widening the slice.
evals.expected_output: Keep the green slice bounded and hand the broader evidence to architecture review for discovery and prioritization.
assertions: Does not widen the completed slice
Names improve-codebase-architecture as the next owner
Carries green-state evidence and candidate scope
Does not assume the candidate is accepted cleanup

evals.name: green-leaves-approved-cleanup
evals.prompt: The behavior change is green and accepted. One separately approved compatibility wrapper and its dead aliases remain, with caller evidence recorded.
evals.expected_output: Hand the green tests and cleanup ledger to structural cleanup; do not keep behavior implementation as owner.
assertions: Names zero-tech-debt as the next owner
Carries green tests, invariants, and deletion evidence
Separates completed behavior work from cleanup
Does not reopen the accepted design

evals.name: accepted-bug-entry
evals.prompt: The expected behavior and public interface for a catalog pagination bug are approved. Fix it test-first.
evals.expected_output: Own the implementation and begin one vertical RED-GREEN slice without asking for duplicate approval.
assertions: Treats tdd-go as the current owner
Does not request approval already present in the handoff
Starts with one observable failing case
